7 Cards Least Official Rules & Scoring Guide

Complete guide to card values, turn flow, discard combinations, Joker wildcards, and penalties.

⚡ What is 7 Cards Least? (Quick Summary)

7 Cards Least (also known as 7 Cards Game, Low Hand Rummy, or Seven Cards Least) is a fast-paced card shedding game played with 7 cards dealt to each player from a standard 52-card deck. The objective is to finish each round with the lowest cumulative hand point total by discarding high-value face cards (10 points each), building matched sets or suited runs, and calling "LEAST!" when your hand total drops to 10 points or fewer.

Card Rank Point Value Shedding Strategy
Ace (A) 1 Point Keep in hand (lowest standard card value)
2 through 10 Face Value (2–10 pts) Discard high numbers (8–10); keep low numbers (2–3)
Jack, Queen, King 10 Points Each Discard immediately in sets or as singles
Table Joker 0 Points Hold (zero-point wildcard for lowest hand score)
Calling Least Threshold ≤ 10 Points Must hold 10 points or less to declare Least
Wrong Call Penalty +80 Points Assessed if an opponent ties or holds a lower hand

1. Deck Setup & Dealing

7 Cards Least is played with a standard 52-card deck without physical jokers. At the start of each round, 7 cards are dealt to each player. One card is flipped face-up in the center to establish the zero-point Table Joker rank for the round, and a second card is flipped face-up to begin the Discard Pile. The remaining undealt cards form the face-down Draw Deck.

2. Card Values & Scoring System

Cards remaining in your hand at the end of a round represent penalty points. The point breakdown is strictly defined:

  • Ace (A): 1 Point.
  • 2 to 10: Face Value (2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10 points).
  • Jack, Queen, King (J, Q, K): 10 Points each.
  • Table Joker Rank: 0 Points (all cards matching the setup card rank count as 0).

3. Valid Discard Combinations & Turn Flow

On your turn, you must discard valid cards onto the Discard Pile before drawing a replacement card. Valid discards include single cards, matching rank sets (e.g. 10♥-10♦), or suited runs of 3+ consecutive cards (e.g. 5♠-6♠-7♠). After discarding, draw one replacement card from either the face-down Draw Deck or top card of the Discard Pile. If your discard matches the current pile top rank, Match & Skip triggers: your turn ends immediately without drawing.

4. Declaring LEAST! & Concrete Penalty Examples

When your total hand score is 10 points or less, you may declare LEAST! during your turn.

Scenario A – Victory: Caller holds 4 points. Opponent holds 9 points. Caller wins the round with 0 penalty points, while opponent scores 5 points (9 − 4).

Scenario B – False Call (80-Point Penalty): Caller declares Least with 7 points, but an opponent holds 5 points! Because the caller did not strictly beat every opponent, the caller incurs the 80-point penalty.
